basis: Positive means strictly greater than zero; relation uniqueness means no repeated key within a fully observed scope. NULL/unavailable and diagnostic codes are declared policy and legacy compatibility expectations, not independent proof that the legacy evaluator or validator is correct. None of these expectations were generated from candidate parser output.
sources: internal/semantic/validationeval/evaluator.go (positive: Sign()>0; nil number is an error; relation-unique: duplicate is not-satisfied, empty scope is satisfied)
internal/validation/semantic_business_validation.go (numeric type requirement, many-relation requirement, duplicate validation identity, attribute ownership)
reference/dsl-language-plugin/relation_match_probe.go (NULL key, unavailable key, unmatched policies have no default)
reference/dsl-language-plugin/operator.go (exact pin; effect other than pure is refused)
internal/syntax/semantic_anchor.go and internal/sourceindex/model.go (byte-offset spans, no re-normalisation)
notes: SF-A/B/C/D are four surfaces for the same two authored rules. Equality claims cover the semantic.Validation value, its logical type, its scope, the presence policy, and the evaluator result distinction. They do NOT cover source bytes, spans, diagnostic positions, formatter output, build artifacts, or owner acceptance.
The rule surface is a candidate parser. It is not wired into workspace.Load, so no accepted Workspace Source changes meaning.
Names such as std.op.positive@1 are fixture labels for comparison, not adopted operator identities.
Evaluation cases use a stub source. No provider, database, or Studio was exercised.

Meaning oracle (positive and uniqueness), policy expectation (NULL/unavailable), and compatibility characterization (diagnostic codes and legacy parser) require different evidence. The fixture does not claim that all test groups are consumed by Go tests.
SF-06 is not equivalent in rule identity: its proposed surface does not declare the expected Validation ID. No implicit ID derivation or Operator pin adoption is authorized.
EX-08 covers an explicitly complete empty stub scope; a physical Provider returning zero rows does not prove scope completeness.
